summary: Iter-58 FriendPlace public website + admin portal backend surface tested end-to-end. 31/32 pytest cases pass in /app/backend/tests/test_iter58_friendplace_public_admin.py against the public preview URL. Covered: (1) GET /api/public/content returns 200 with all six documented keys (about, features, faqs, founders, success_stories, download); a single site_content doc keyed 'main' is seeded on first call and re-reads produce byte-identical JSON, confirming idempotent seeding; the endpoint is reachable from Origin: https://friendplace.com.au (allow-origin honoured — see finding below). (2) GET /api/public/founders/count returns {count: <int>} matching the live count of non-demo is_founder:true users (currently 4). (3) POST /api/public/contact — valid payload persists a status:'new' doc, missing message → 400, invalid email 'noatsign' → 400, email is normalised to lowercase, DB write happens even when the Resend call rate-limits (verified via backend logs: 'email.send failed: Too many requests' followed by HTTP 200 to the caller — failure-tolerance property is confirmed). (4) All four admin endpoints (analytics/summary, analytics/growth, analytics/engagement, contact-submissions) reject INVALID_UUID and the non-admin real user (realtest1) with 403 and accept the maggie admin_id with 200 — 12/12 parametrised auth-guard checks pass. (5) /analytics/summary returns all 10 documented keys as ints; /analytics/growth?days=7 returns exactly 7 zero-filled ascending YYYY-MM-DD buckets; /analytics/engagement satisfies dau<=wau<=mau. (6) Full contact-submission lifecycle verified: submit → appears in status=new list → PATCH to 'replied' → 200 → no longer in status=new list → DB status field is 'replied'. PATCH with status='pizza' → 400. PATCH with unknown id → 404. PATCH still requires admin_id (non-admin → 403). (7) Regression spot-checks: /api/ root, /api/health, /api/users/{id} (auth-gated 401 as expected), /api/admin/invite-flyer (returns 1240x1754 PNG), /api/auth/signup — all still work. ONE FAILURE: the 6-per-hour per-IP rate limit on /api/public/contact does NOT trigger a 429 because request.client.host in this deployment resolves to the k8s ingress pod IP (10.227.37.2 or 10.227.37.5, alternating) — see backend_issues.critical. Also flagged: the k8s ingress overrides the FastAPI CORS middleware and returns 'access-control-allow-origin: *' + 'access-control-allow-credentials: true' regardless of the whitelist in server.py:9263-9277 — the marketing site will work but credentialed cross-origin admin calls could be browser-rejected in production if cookies/Authorization headers are added.

critical.issue: IP-based rate limit is effectively bypassed behind the k8s ingress. request.client.host returns the ingress pod IP (observed: 10.227.37.2 and 10.227.37.5) which rotates round-robin across ingress replicas, so the same real client can trivially exceed the 5/hour cap. Fix: derive the client IP from the X-Forwarded-For header (leftmost hop) with request.client.host as fallback. Reference: server.py:8912.

minor.issue: The k8s ingress strips FastAPI's CORS response headers and rewrites 'access-control-allow-origin' to '*' AND still sets 'access-control-allow-credentials: true'. This combo is browser-invalid for credentialed cross-origin requests. The current public marketing endpoints don't need credentials so functionality is fine, but the explicit whitelist Garry added (friendplace.com.au, www.friendplace.com.au, admin.friendplace.com.au) is inert at the ingress layer. Verify with: curl -sI -H 'Origin: https://evil.example.com' <base>/api/public/founders/count — evil origin still receives allow-origin:*. Ingress config change is likely needed for the admin portal to send Authorization headers safely.

action_items: HIGH: Replace `ip = (request.client.host if request and request.client else 'unknown')` in the contact endpoint (server.py:8912) with an X-Forwarded-For derivation. Suggested: xff = request.headers.get('x-forwarded-for', '').split(',')[0].strip(); ip = xff or (request.client.host if request.client else 'unknown'). This will restore the 5/hour cap that the current code silently loses behind the k8s ingress. Confirmed reproducer in the test suite (TestContactSubmission::test_rate_limit_returns_429_on_sixth logs distinct ingress IPs in its failure message).

MEDIUM: Investigate the k8s ingress CORS override. FastAPI is trying to echo the whitelisted origin, but the ingress replaces it with '*' + 'allow-credentials: true' — this combination is rejected by browsers for credentialed requests. If the admin portal ever needs to send Authorization headers, either (a) drop credentials mode client-side (still fine — auth is admin_id query/body param today), or (b) reconfigure the ingress to pass through the FastAPI-set headers, or (c) accept the '*' as the intentional preview-env behavior and document it. No code change in server.py fixes this — it's an infra concern.

LOW/OPTIONAL: Consider adding an index on contact_submissions.{ip: 1, created_at: -1} once the X-Forwarded-For fix is in — the current count_documents scan is fine at 6 rows but will not scale past a few thousand submissions.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:8912 — Uses request.client.host as the sole IP source. In every real deployment behind a load-balancer/ingress (including this preview), this is the LB pod IP, not the caller. This silently defeats the rate limiter described in the doc-comment on line 8909. Must switch to X-Forwarded-For.

server.py:8849 — _get_site_content_doc pops _id and key AFTER returning from the find call, but the initial insert on line 8853 uses `dict(doc)` (a shallow copy). Good — pymongo's insert_one mutates its argument to add _id, but the copy protects the returned dict. Verified idempotent by test.
server.py:8918 — Rate limit boundary is `recent >= 5`, i.e. the 6th submission is blocked. Matches the review request. Documented correctly.

server.py:8939-8954 — Email send is wrapped in try/except and never raises through to the caller. Confirmed by backend logs: multiple 'email.send failed: Too many requests' warnings were observed during testing while the endpoint continued to return 200 to the client. Failure-tolerance property is intact.

server.py:8969-9001 (analytics/summary) — All 10 keys resolved via a helper that swallows count_documents exceptions and returns 0. This is fine for a dashboard where a stale zero is better than a 500. All keys are cast to int() explicitly. Good.

server.py:9018-9022 (analytics/growth) — Uses $substr on the ISO string prefix. Works only because the schema convention is to always store created_at as ISO-8601 strings; a Date-type document would silently produce empty buckets. Not a bug given the codebase convention, but worth a comment.

server.py:9056-9065 (analytics/engagement) — Fall-back to updated_at is only applied when last_active is missing, not when it's null. In practice this is fine, but consider {'$or': [{'last_active': {'$gt': cutoff}}, {'last_active': {'$in': [None, '']}, 'updated_at': {'$gt': cutoff}}]} for slightly more robust old-schema handling.
server.py:9099-9100 (PATCH contact-submissions) — Correctly rejects unknown status values with 400 (raises before the update). Uses `.lower()` on the input which is friendly. Good.

server.py:9263-9277 — CORS whitelist correctly adds the three friendplace.com.au origins. The env-var override (CORS_ORIGINS) is respected. Whitelist is functionally inert behind the current k8s ingress (see minor issue above), but the code is correct.

server.py file size is now 9346 lines — well past the 700-line ceiling from the code review guidelines. Not this iteration's problem, but worth flagging for the next refactor: the file should be split into `routes/public.py`, `routes/admin_analytics.py`, `routes/admin_contact.py` etc. Not urgent.

rca_of_issue: PRIMARY BUG — rate limit bypass. RCA: /api/public/contact computes the client IP as `request.client.host`. In a Kubernetes ingress deployment this is the socket peer address, which is the ingress-controller pod's IP. There are (at least) two ingress replicas in the preview cluster (10.227.37.2 and 10.227.37.5); nginx-ingress and cloud LBs load-balance across them, so consecutive requests from a single real client arrive at the backend with rotating source IPs. The count_documents({ip: <one_of_them>}) filter therefore only sees ~half the true submission volume, and the 5/hour cap becomes ~10/hour per real client — trivially bypassable. Reproduction: run the failing test — the assertion message lists the two ingress pod IPs harvested from the last 6 submissions' persisted `ip` field. Mitigation: parse X-Forwarded-For (already set by the k8s ingress to the real client IP). Suggested one-line change: `ip = (request.headers.get('x-forwarded-for','').split(',')[0].strip() or (request.client.host if request.client else 'unknown'))`. SECONDARY FINDING — CORS override. RCA: the FastAPI CORSMiddleware sets an origin-specific header, but the k8s ingress rewrites the response with allow-origin:* and allow-credentials:true. Not a server.py bug; infra layer needs configuration or the credentials mode needs to be disabled client-side. Functional impact today is zero for public marketing endpoints; potential future impact for the admin portal only if it moves to cookie/Authorization-based CORS calls.
